the VACS Index is a useful tool for predicting everyday functioning problems in persons living with HIV.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VACS Index is a useful tool for predicting everyday functioning in HIV-infected patients.
the VACS index is a composite marker that is associated with everyday functioning among HIV infected individuals.
the VACS Index and NCI are independent correlates of everyday functioning, and that the two should be considered together in clinical practice and future research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV disease severity, as reflected by the VACS index, is associated with everyday functioning problems among HIV-infected adults after accounting for NCI and other well-established predictors.
HIV-infected persons who have worse physical health, worse neurocognitive impairment, and/or more psychiatric comorbidity are at increased risk for everyday functioning difficulties.

a composite marker of health, like the VACS Index or the Charlson Index, can be a useful tool in identifying persons with HIV at risk for functional impairment and may be a good candidate for inclusion as an additional predictor of functional outcomes in clinical trials of HIV treatments.
